ai.title: browseraction auto-screenshots, viewport config, spinner UX
ai.summary: browser_action now returns a screenshot after navigate actions, replacing empty responses. Viewport dimensions moved from hardcoded 1200x800 to BROWSER_DEFAULTS.viewportWidth/Height (1280x720) in common/src/browser-actions.ts. Spinner added to tool-handlers.ts during browser actions for visual feedback. System prompt updated to encourage proactive browser observation and require explicit type field in action parameters.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to look at a web page, it now shows you a picture of the page right after it lands on it, instead of going dark and leaving you wondering what it saw. The assistant's instructions also nudge it toward actually peeking at the screen and describing what it sees, rather than guessing. Finally, while a page is loading you\'ll now see a little spinning indicator so you know the assistant is working instead of frozen. These improvements are live today.

eli5.text: The assistant has been quietly updated and is now live for everyone using it. Behind the scenes, it can now think with Google's newest AI model, Gemini 2.0, which makes its answers a bit smarter and faster. The assistant is also better at picking out which files you actually need it to look at, so it won't get confused or miss important details as easily. Everything should just feel a little more reliable when you ask it for help.

Changes confined to web/src/app/docs/layout.tsx, web/src/components/docs/doc-sidebar.tsx, and web/src/components/docs/mdx/code-demo.tsx. Copy button now uses native button element with aria-label and hover opacity transitions.

eli5.text: When you browse the documentation on a computer, the page now has a bit more breathing room around the text and the left-hand menu, and the menu item for the page you're on is a touch easier to spot. On a phone, the copy-code button on code examples now works like a regular button and hides until you point at it, then shows a checkmark when you've copied. The mobile menu at the bottom of the screen also looks a little cleaner and sits behind a soft, blurred strip so the content below doesn't fight for your attention. These are small visual polish touches, and they're live today.

ai.summary: getProjectFileTreePrompt accepts mode param. Search/agent contexts pass distinct strings. Agent mode adds ignore instruction. Reorders shouldAddFilePlaceholders args.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal file overview now comes in two flavors. When helping with web searches, it shows your project files normally; when writing or editing code, it adds a reminder to ignore irrelevant files. The behind-the-scenes plumbing that decides when to show placeholder comments in your files was also reorganized for clarity, but this doesn't change what you see or experience.

eli5.text: The assistant stopped using special placeholder words like '[FILE_IGNORED]' and '[ERROR_LOADING_FILE]' to mark files it skipped during loading. Instead, it now simply treats those files as empty (null) and, for the planning step, drops any file whose content is either missing or longer than 400,000 characters. You wouldn't directly notice this unless you were looking at how the system handles large or ignored files when building a plan, where the behavior stays the same but the internal logic is cleaner.

If you looked at the configuration files, you would see one collection no longer has a now-removed money-tracking script and is marked as private, another has a new building command, and the shared utilities section gained a short description and its own type-checking step. ai.title: Refine agent prompts to reduce unnecessary code edits
ai.summary: Updated `main-prompt.ts` to instruct the agent to briefly summarize actions rather than review and improve implementation. `system-prompt.ts` response format now explicitly branches into answering questions (1a), planning (1b), or other modes, preventing unsolicited code changes during brainstorming. Tool call syntax rules were tightened to prevent nesting within `<edit_file>` blocks. These changes aim to align agent output with user intent, avoiding accidental modifications when only explanation or review is requested.

eli5.text: The assistant that helps work on the software now keeps its responses shorter and more focused, so it won't surprise you by editing code when you only asked questions or wanted a quick plan. It also now clearly separates answering questions, planning next steps, or doing other kinds of work, rather than jumping straight into changing code. If you interact with it, you'll notice its replies stick to what you actually asked for instead of over-explaining or rewriting things you didn't request, and tool usage rules were tightened so actions don't accidentally get nested inside file editing commands.

ai.title: Add pre/post browser action screenshots with backend limits
ai.summary: Browser actions now capture optional JPEG screenshots before and after execution, gated by an active page session. The backend enforces a limit of two screenshots per request via `limitScreenshots` in `common/util/messages.ts`, applied specifically in `backend/src/claude.ts` for Sonnet models. Haiku, Deepseek, and Gemini transformers strip image content or convert formats to ensure compatibility with providers lacking native image support. Failure to capture screenshots logs a warning or error but does not halt execution.

eli5.text: When you ask the AI to use a computer (like clicking buttons or typing), it can now optionally take up to two pictures of your screen to show what happened before and after each step. These pictures, which look like regular screen photos, only appear when the AI is actively controlling a browser session and only the highest-tier models like Sonnet can receive them; other models automatically strip out the images so they don't break. If a picture fails to take for any reason, the AI just quietly logs a note and keeps going without stopping, so your task won't crash even if screenshots miss.

ai.title: Fix Claude cost tracking calculations
ai.summary: Restores accurate cost tracking by capturing cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens from Anthropic stream usage data. Previously, these fields were omitted from saveMessage calls, leading to incomplete billing records. The fix updates backend/src/claude.ts to extract and persist these specific token counts alongside standard input/output metrics.

eli5.text: The system that records how much it costs to talk to the AI assistant now captures the full picture of the conversation, including parts that were reused from earlier in the chat. When the assistant responds, all the token counts, including the reusable cache portions, are now saved, so billing records match what Anthropic actually returned. You won't see this directly, but it fixes undercounted usage so the costs add up correctly behind the scenes.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer has instructions telling it to look up and run custom build scripts that live inside a project's configuration file. If you watched closely, you would notice the assistant skips a whole category of actions it used to consider, namely checking the list of available scripts and being told to ask before running any with lasting effects. Who it affects: anyone giving tasks to the assistant today. What you would notice: the assistant won't offer to run those scripts or warn about their permanent side effects.

ai.title: Backend token count cache reduced to 1000 entries
ai.summary: The backend token counter now limits `TOKEN_COUNT_CACHE` to 1000 entries, down from 5000. The change is in `backend/src/util/token-counter.ts`, where the `LRUCache<string, number>` capacity was reduced. It affects cached token-count results for strings.

eli5.text: When the assistant figures out how many tokens are in a piece of text, it saves that result so it doesn't have to calculate it again. Those saved results are now kept in a smaller list of 1000 recent items instead of 5000, which means older, less frequently used token counts will be dropped sooner. If you interact with longer or more varied text prompts, you might notice slightly slower responses when those prompts haven't been seen before. This change is live today in the backend service.

constants.name: TOKEN_COUNT_CACHE
constants.from: new LRUCache<string, number>(5000) // Cache up to 5k strings

ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts gains a cleanup directive. Agent must add imports, remove unused vars/functions/files, and delete replaced code. Scope: system prompt text only.

eli5.text: The system added a new rule to its internal instruction manual that tells it to clean up after itself whenever it makes changes: it must add any new pieces it needs, remove any leftover parts it no longer uses, and delete older code that has been replaced. This only affects how the assistant behaves behind the scenes when editing, so you won't see any visible change in your experience today, but it should help keep things tidy and avoid broken or unused pieces piling up in the background.

ai.title: Refactor LLM provider stream handlers
ai.summary: Refactored `claude.ts`, `deepseek-api.ts`, and `gemini-api.ts` to destructure options and standardize error handling in stream generators. Removed redundant try/finally blocks in `claude.ts` and normalized variable usage across providers. Updated `billing.knowledge.md` with cache cost analysis and API error handling best practices, specifically regarding retries and stream cleanup.

eli5.text: The way the system talks to three different AI services (Anthropic's Claude, DeepSeek, and Google's Gemini) got a tidy-up behind the scenes, the code that handles live text streams from each was simplified and made consistent, redundant cleanup steps were removed, and error handling was made more reliable. This is internal housekeeping: if you're a subscriber, you won't see new features, but the assistant should be a bit more stable and predictable when streaming responses. The team also added notes about how caching costs work and how to properly retry failed API calls, so future billing and reliability issues get handled better.
